about.title: Hero Grid Tool
about.whatIs.p1: **Hero Grid Tool** is an "alt-tab" tool for building and customizing Dota 2 hero layouts -- a personal notebook to manage your game vision.
about.whatIs.p2: Use the [Edit](/edit) tab to build a grid: add categories, fill them with heroes and items from the adding dialog or by dragging portraits around, then rename, recolour and resize them. You can even link them together so that they will stay this way even if you look at them on a smaller screen. The [View](/view) tab is the clean read-only version you keep next to the game, and [Grids](/layouts) holds every grid you have saved.
about.whatIs.p2_1: Aside from static grid, it also supports a Canvas mode, which is the closest you can get to the in-game hero grid. You can also import in-game grids or export them from this tool for the game.
about.whatIs.p3: Everything lives in your browser's local storage, nothing is uploaded. You can sync the grids by saving them as files or using a share link (or QR).
about.building.categories: **Categories** hold heroes, items, empty slots and row breaks. Each one can override the grid's portrait style, size and item icons. You can also add a hero icon/portrait or an item to the category name.
about.building.chains: **Chains** keep categories together: link them horizontally (adjacent columns) or vertically (stacked rows) with the ↔ and ↕ buttons. A category can be in both.
about.building.breaks: **Row breaks** split a category's portraits onto a new line.
about.building.labels: **Labels** can be free text, one of the presets (lanes, positions, roles, tiers) or a hero/item/facet icon -- optionally with a colour tag.
about.building.columns: The column count adapts to the window: a narrow screen caps the number of columns so categories stay readable.
about.autogrid.intro: The **Autogrid** tab generates stats-based meta tier lists based on [Spectral Stats Hub](https://stats.spectral.gg). You can use ranked/competitive meta or choose a custom report tag (e.g. tournament or an old patch).
about.autogrid.roleGrids: **Role grids** -- one tier per row, coloured by tier.
about.autogrid.total: **Total meta** -- a column per role, a tier per row.
about.autogrid.overall: **Overall tier list** -- the same six tiers with no role split, one row each.
about.autogrid.metaLevels: **Meta levels** -- the report's meta layers, oldest first.
about.autogrid.personalIntro: Provide your Steam Account ID with a public match history open to generate a hero grid based you the current meta adjusted for your playstyle. Three things move a hero: how you perform with it and how much you play it.
about.autogrid.best: **Best heroes** -- the ones you are known for.
about.autogrid.practice: **Practice** -- strong heroes you need to practice.
about.autogrid.bans: **Bans** -- the heroes with the best record against you.
about.autogrid.roles: **Roles** -- one block each, best-for-you first, optionally ordered by how much you play the roles.
about.keys.intro: Every shortcut is **Alt** plus one key, and none of them fire while you are typing in a field.
about.formats.intro: The tool reads every format below, so paste it into [Grids -> Import](/layouts), drop in a file, or scan a QR code. Imports are detected automatically, so you never have to say which kind it is.
about.formats.codeP: A single grid is packed into a binary record, compressed with gzip, and written as URL-safe base64 -- typically around a hundred characters, but it might be more if you make use of the custom text labels. Compression is only kept when it actually makes the code shorter. The record is, in order:
about.formats.f2: `flags` -- one byte of board toggles: colourful labels, centered, darkened background, freeform canvas, transparent categories.
about.formats.f4: `name`, `icon`, `author`, `description` -- length-prefixed UTF-8 strings (author and description may be empty).
about.formats.f5: `categories` -- a count, then one record per category: flags, label (preset id or text), optional icon, colour, width, header size, chain ids, per-category style overrides, and finally its elements.
about.formats.f6: `elements` -- one byte of kind and flags each, plus a hero/item id, a custom tag, or nothing for empty slots and row breaks.
about.formats.allP: Your whole collection can be exported at once. That is the JSON list below, deflated and base64 encoded, as used by **Share all** and `/layouts?l=<code>`.
about.formats.jsonP: The `.json` export is human-readable and diff-friendly -- a saved grid, or a list of them:
about.formats.jsonNote: A bare `board` object works too. Hero and item `refId`s are the standard Dota ids, `preset` replaces `text` for preset labels, and `hGroup` / `vGroup` mark chained categories.
about.formats.gameP: The game's own `hero_grid_config.json` is read and written as-is, making the best effort to preserve the most information you have here.
about.sharing.link: **Link** -- the grid code in a URL, plus a QR code for getting it onto a phone.
about.sharing.image: **Image** -- a PNG of the whole grid, 1600px wide, with the grid name, author, description and a QR code linking back to the editable version.
about.sharing.print: **Print** -- Ctrl+P lays the grid out on one page, on white, with the same banner as the image.
about.sharing.files: **Files** -- `.txt` for a code, `.json` for one grid or all of them.
about.credits.dev: Original design, structure, technical plan and implementation by [Leamare](https://spectral.gg), ported to new framework and implemented the rest of the features with some LLM assistance.
about.credits.inspired: Inspired by [reddit post by TorteDeLini](https://www.reddit.com/r/DotA2/comments/7iurzb/i_started_creating_a_drafting_chart_around_my/). Metadata and images are from [spectral courier](https://spectral.gg/reshub).

whatsnew.title: What's new in {version}
whatsnew.intro: The Hero Grid Tool has been rebuilt from scratch. Everything is faster, the layout engine is new, and grids now travel as compact codes instead of long blobs.
whatsnew.migrated: Your grids from the previous version were converted and are waiting in [Grids](/layouts). Portrait styles and item settings use the new defaults — adjust them in the sidebar.
whatsnew.items: **Items** can go on the grid alongside heroes, with inventory or profile-badge icons.
whatsnew.chains: **Chained categories** — link categories horizontally or vertically and they stay together as the grid reflows.
whatsnew.breaks: **Row breaks** inside a category, so you can group portraits into rows.
whatsnew.images: **Shareable images** — export the whole grid as a PNG with a QR code, author and description.
whatsnew.portable: **Portable grids** — copy a grid code, save it as a file, and import codes, JSON or files exported from the old version.
whatsnew.misc: Alternate hero portraits, category icons, colour tags, more preset labels and tier labels, drag-and-drop everywhere, and five interface languages.
whatsnew.seeAbout: See [About](/about) for the supported grid formats.

game.replaceSame: Replace grids with the same name
game.replaceHint: Otherwise an imported grid whose name already exists is kept alongside it, stamped with the import time.
game.exportNote: In-game grids only store hero positions, so items, alternate portraits and colours are dropped. A category icon travels as {S:spectre}, and a row break splits the category into blocks named ------ — both are restored if you import the file back here.
